description: gaia is an R empirical model that estimates annual crop-yield shocks under changing weather and carbon-dioxide conditions. Its developers use published econometric response surfaces for 17 crops and monthly temperature and precipitation projections to produce country-level shocks suitable for multisectoral models. The JOSS paper and own repository identify the package; the R DESCRIPTION states BSD-3-Clause, so the code is free. Spatial output is national and temporal output annual, even when source climate data are gridded and monthly. Food-supply and irrigation modellers could use shocks as scenario inputs when testing production losses or trade responses. A caveat is that aggregation obscures local extremes, and yield response depends on historical relationships, climate bias correction and assumptions about adaptation. gaia does not model a farm or prove future harvests. No directly related catalogue record was established. The article and own package metadata were read without obtaining climate products or running a projection.
inputs: Historical crop yields and climate response surfaces
name: gaia crop yield climate response
notes: G5 G5-0834. Software checked through metadata and documentation, without installation or execution. Geographic scope follows the documented application or software portability; it does not imply validation throughout that area.
